assumptions.obligation: No request (i_a_valid = 0) while rst_ni is asserted.
TL-UL host rule: once i_a_valid is high, it stays high and every A-channel input stays stable until o_a_ready. This covers opcode, param, size, source, address, mask, data, instr and intg_flip.
No PutFullData or PutPartialData request with i_a_instr = 1.
A new request does not reuse the a_source of a request that is still outstanding. A source is freed by its D-channel handshake, including one in the same cycle, or by reset.
No full-mask write to ALERT_TEST (0x0) that sets fatal_fault = 1 with regwen = 0, i.e. the combined write 0x0000_0001. Tests write 0x8000_0001 instead.

Full-word writes with good integrity to CFG0 (0x10C), TIMER_V_LOWER0 (0x110) or TIMER_V_UPPER0 (0x114) happen only while CTRL.active_0 is 0. A shadow copy of CTRL tracks this from the testbench's own accepted CTRL writes.

notes:
Not constrained on purpose. The spec makes these legal stimulus that the DUT must detect and answer with d_error (RT-4.1-05, RT-7-07):
- a_opcode, a_size and a_mask (undefined opcodes, bad sizes, non-contiguous or partial masks)
- misaligned addresses and unmapped offsets below 0x200
- i_a_intg_flip (integrity faults)
- i_a_instr on Get (instruction-fetch reads)
- i_d_ready (D-channel back-pressure)

Software guidance such as RT-T4.2-06 (write mtimecmp after mtime) does not oblige the bus, so it is not assumed. No minimum reset length is assumed (TL-T3.1.1-02).

ENV-08 shadow of CTRL: it updates when the testbench's full-mask CTRL write is accepted on the A channel, not when the write completes. A full-mask CTRL write counts even if its a_size is wrong, so it slightly over-approximates whether the timer is active. That is slightly too strict, but it can never wrongly allow a write while the timer runs. Sub-word or integrity-corrupted writes to CFG0/TIMER_V stay allowed while the timer is active, so the error-and-no-effect behaviour is still checked.

Not yet run through Yosys or a solver.
